text:
maria: quick heads-up — p99 on a subset of pods jumped from 420ms -> ~1.6s starting 03/12. correlated with long prompts and tool-calls (reranker -> external).
kevin: do we have a reproducible trace? sample ids/req ids?
jin: I pulled a few traces, attaching minimal profiler snippet below. looks like KV cache miss + kernel hop for some sequences.
maria: sharing two traces: req 9f3a and req b12c. both long context (~8k tokens) and a couple of tool-call retries.
kevin: can you paste the hot stack from the pprof?
jin: sure — key bits:
```
# pprof top
1.2s  (45%)  inference.exec -> attention_kernel_select
0.8s  (30%)  kv_cache::fetch_miss -> recompute_prefix_states
0.5s  (19%)  batching::microbatch_wait -> wait_for_batch_slot
0.1s  (6%)  rpc::tool_call -> external_timeout
```
sam: interesting — attention_kernel_select high % only for those long sequences. might be selecting a fallback kernel for very large seq-lengths. kernel-selector logs?
maria: yes, kernel-selector switched to classic GEMM path at seq_len>4096 for that model on these hosts.
kevin: that change was rolled in the 03/10 kernel heuristics tweak (PR #4521) — it biases towards conservative kernels to avoid OOM.
jin: hypothesis: conservative kernel + KV miss causes recompute on long prefixes, which increases per-token latency and amplifies tail when tool-calls interleave and block batching.
maria: that matches the traces: recompute_prefix_states spikes right before tool_call, then batch slots pile up waiting for KV warmup.
sam: can we bisect microbatch sizing? maybe larger microbatch would amortize kernel overhead for long seqs. but that will hurt SLO for short queries.
kevin: run quick experiment: on a canary pool, set microbatch_target=8 -> 16 for requests with seq_len>2048, and increase KV prefetch probability for starts of tool-calls. we can toggle via rollout config.
maria: started a canary at 2049991130 — will monitor p95/p99 and throughput.
jin: two more quick checks: 1) are tool-call retries spinning (causing loops)? 2) do we have skewed RNGs producing longer-than-expected generations? logs show a handful of outliers with repeated tool invocations in <200ms loops.
sam: ops-bot reports 6 retries for external-service x in that window. @ops-bot can you paste the external error rates?
ops-bot: external-service-x: error_rate 0.4% (baseline 0.05%), avg latency 320ms -> 780ms during spike window.
kevin: external errors explain tool-call waits. tool-call blocking holding up microbatch fill -> batching stalls -> kernel selection sees odd sequence lengths -> fallback kernels -> recompute. cascade.
maria: early canary results: p95 stable, p99 down 18% on canary nodes but throughput delta -6%.
jin: can we try optimistic kernel path for those canary nodes but with stricter OOM guard (OOM kill metrics + soft-failover)? if kernel works most of the time we'll get latency wins.
sam: +1. also add KV prewarm for contexts that are tool-call heavy (mark session metadata).
kevin: plan: 1) increase microbatch_target for seq>2048 on canary 2) enable optimistic kernel selector with soft-fallback 3) bump KV prefetch for tool-call sessions 4) add short-circuit timeout for tool-call retries (cut after 2 retries). roll tomorrow if canary looks good.
maria: logging checklist to capture if we roll: kernel_choice, kv_fetch_hit, microbatch_size_at_dispatch, tool_call_retries, external_latency.
jin: I'll add a small perf test to emulate tool-call loops (internal harness) — should catch regressions.
sam: thanks — once tests land let's correlate with cost delta. we care p99 recovery without >10% throughput loss.
kevin: noted. I'll also add alert on kernel-selector flip-rate per host — sudden flips are a smell.
maria: ok thanks all. will update thread with canary metrics in ~30m. :thumbsup:
